:::{#thm-tm-robustness}
#### The details of the model change running time only polynomially

Let $f$ be a function from $\set{0, 1}^*$ to $\set{0, 1}^*$,
and let $T$ be [time-constructible](#def-time-constructible).
Suppose a [Turing machine](#def-turing-machine) $M$ with $k$ tapes and an alphabet of $s$ symbols
[computes](#def-tm-computes) $f$ in time $T(n)$.
Then:

1. A Turing machine with $k$ tapes and the alphabet $\set{0, 1, \square, \triangleright}$
   computes $f$ in time $\asymub{T(n) \log_2 s}$.
2. A single-tape machine computes $f$ in time $\asymub{T(n)^2}$.
3. If $M$ is instead a bidirectional machine,
   a Turing machine computes $f$ in time $\asymub{T(n)}$.

A *single-tape machine* is the same as a Turing machine,
except that it has one tape, which starts with $\triangleright$ followed by the input,
which it can read and write,
and which holds the output when it [halts](#def-turing-machine).
A *bidirectional machine* is the same as a Turing machine,
except that each tape also goes on forever to the left of the cell holding $\triangleright$,
and a head can move left from that cell.
The input and the output sit to the right of $\triangleright$, as before.
The constant in part 2 depends on $k$,
and none of the constants depends on $f$, $T$, or $n$
[@arora2009computational, section 1.3].

:::
